newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Colombo tea auction prices rise after holidays.
newsitem.headline: Colombo tea auction prices rise after holidays.

text.p: Prices of most grades of Sri Lanka tea rose at the Colombo auction on Wednesday on good widespread demand, brokers said.

"The auction took off to a fairly good start after the (traditional) new year holidays. Other than a small selection of teas which were lower, most prices were higher," said a broker at Forbes and Walker. "Perhaps the one-week break helped. Also it was a small sale."
The anticipated gross auction average price for the 3.7 million kg on offer rose to 111 rupees ($1.89) per kg from 110.85 rupees previously, Forbes and Walker said.

Better Western BOPs were two to three rupees lower while BOPFs were three to five rupees dearer. Better Uva BOPs were two to four rupees lower while most other Uva/Udapussellwa BOP/BOPFs were three to five rupees dearer.
Among low growns, the mainstay of the auction, select best leafy teas, though irregular, were generally firm. Others gained three to five rupees and more.

The auction was not held last week because of the traditional new year on April 13-14 and holidays.The next auction is on April 29-30 when 4.7 million kg will be on offer. ($1=58.86 rupees) --Colombo newsroom (941) 434319
